newsitem.title: GERMANY: German intervention grain offers fail to pick up.
newsitem.headline: German intervention grain offers fail to pick up.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season continued to lag those in the same 1995/96 period, figures from the state grain intervention board BLE showed.
Volumes on January 10 totalled 331,498 tonnes compared with 1,184,133 a year earlier.
The figure described volumes accepted by stores by the close last Friday.
Market prices of wheat and barley had been lifted by export sales and domestic demand, and had held above the January intervention buying-in price of 238.10 marks a tonne, traders said.
Some feed rye and barley was sold to northern and eastern German intervention stores but at a slower pace than in December.
